## CF

[`CF`](https://vedicreader.github.io/cfeasy/core.html#cf) holds one
connection to the Cloudflare API and offers a method for each job. The
token comes from the `token` argument, or from the
`CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` environment variable when you leave it out.
`timeout` is the number of seconds to wait for each request, and any
other keyword arguments go straight to the SDK’s `Cloudflare` client.

Every method returns plain dictionaries and lists, converted from the
SDK’s objects. These results print and serialise without extra work.

The methods come in three groups:

- Zones and DNS records: `zones`, `zone_id`, `dns_records`,
  `create_record`, `delete_record` and `upsert_record`. A zone is a
  domain you manage on Cloudflare. The low-level methods take a zone ID;
  `upsert_record` takes the domain name and looks the ID up itself. Use
  it in most code.
- Tunnels: `account_id`, `tunnels`, `tunnel_id`, `create_tunnel`,
  `delete_tunnel`, `tunnel_token` and `tunnel_cname`. Tunnels belong to
  an account rather than a zone. `tunnels`, `tunnel_id`,
  `create_tunnel`, `delete_tunnel` and `tunnel_token` take an optional
  `account_id` and use your first account when you leave it out.
  `tunnel_cname` writes the DNS record that points a name at a tunnel. A
  CNAME cannot share a name with an A or AAAA record, so it deletes
  those two types at the name first and leaves every other type alone.
- Shortcuts: `verify` checks the token without changing anything, and
  `setup_tunnel` creates a tunnel, its DNS record and its token in one
  call.

`upsert_record` keeps one record of the given type per name and never
touches records of other types, so a TXT or MX record beside an A record
survives. Among the existing records of that type, one with the same
content is kept, otherwise the first; it is updated in place when its
content or `proxied` setting differs, and the other records of that type
are deleted. If there is none, the record is created. A name is read as
a subdomain of the domain unless it already ends in the domain; `@` and
the domain itself mean the apex, and a trailing dot is ignored.

`verify` confirms the token works before you change anything. It checks
that the token is active, that it can see an account, its zones (or the
one zone named by `domain`) and that account’s tunnels. It returns `ok`,
the token status, the account ID, the zone names, the tunnel count and
an `errors` dict naming each check that failed. Account-owned tokens are
checked against the account endpoint. The examples below ran against a
real account and are not run by the docs build. The second
`setup_tunnel` call serves the domain `sankalpa.sh` itself instead of a
subdomain.

``` python
class Pg(list):
    "SDK pages are truthy even when empty."
    def __bool__(self): return True

def fake_cf(status='active', zones=('example.com',), accts=('acc1',), user_tok=True):
    c = CF('x'); m = c._c = MagicMock()
    v = NS(id='t1', status=status)
    if user_tok: m.user.tokens.verify.return_value = v
    else: m.user.tokens.verify.side_effect = Exception('Invalid API Token')
    m.accounts.tokens.verify.return_value = v
    m.accounts.list.side_effect = lambda: Pg(NS(id=a) for a in accts)
    m.zones.list.side_effect = lambda name=None: Pg(NS(id=f'z-{z}', name=z, model_dump=lambda z=z: dict(name=z)) for z in zones if name in (None, z))
    m.zero_trust.tunnels.cloudflared.list.side_effect = lambda account_id: Pg()
    return c
```

### Cache rules and purges

A ruleset is a list of Cloudflare rules. A phase identifies when
Cloudflare applies a ruleset. The entrypoint ruleset is the ruleset that
a zone configures for one phase. A zone keeps its cache rules and its
custom firewall rules in entrypoint rulesets.

`ruleset_upsert` puts your `rules` into the entrypoint ruleset for
`phase`. A `ref` is the stable identifier that `ruleset_upsert` uses to
match a rule. Give each rule a stable `ref`. The function keeps every
rule whose `ref` is absent from your input, with all its keys, such as
`logging` or `ratelimit`. The update omits Cloudflare’s read-only fields
`version`, `last_updated` and `categories`. The function compares the
rules that have your refs with your rules on the keys `description`,
`expression`, `action`, `action_parameters` and `enabled`, and on every
other key that your rules set. It returns `False` and sends nothing when
the compared keys match. Otherwise it writes the merged list and returns
`True`. Running it on every deploy is safe. The token needs Zone -\>
Cache Rules -\> Edit for the cache phase, and Zone -\> Zone WAF -\> Edit
for `http_request_firewall_custom`.

`purge` empties the zone’s cache by URL `files`, by URL `prefixes`, or
`everything`. Files and prefixes go in separate requests, files first,
because the API takes one kind per request. `tries` limits the total
number of attempts for one request. `wait` sets the delay in seconds
before the first retry. Each later delay is twice the previous delay.
The table shows how `purge` treats each failure.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Failure</th>
<th>Treatment</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>HTTP 408, HTTP 409, HTTP 429, Cloudflare code 1134, any HTTP 5xx, or
a connection error such as a timeout</td>
<td>Retry, up to <code>tries</code> attempts</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>HTTP 403, or HTTP 400 whose message names the plan or a
permission</td>
<td>Refusal: raise, or purge everything when
<code>fallback_all=True</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Any other error, including a retryable failure that outlasts the
retries</td>
<td>Raise and purge nothing more</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

By default, `purge` raises the refusal caused by a plan or permission
restriction and purges nothing more. `fallback_all` defaults to `False`.
Set `fallback_all=True` to request a full purge after the refusal. A
full purge empties the whole zone cache, and the origin serves every
request until the cache refills. The return value lists the purge
requests that succeeded. After a fallback, the list holds the files
purge when it ran first, then the purge of everything. A caller can tell
from this list when the fallback ran.

### CF.ruleset_upsert

``` python
def ruleset_upsert(
    zid, rules, phase:str='http_request_cache_settings'
)->bool:
```

*Put `rules` in the zone entrypoint for `phase`, replacing the rules
with the same `ref` and keeping the rest whole; False when nothing
changed.*

``` python
def fake_rules(rules=()):
    c, calls = CF('x'), []
    R = lambda d: NS(model_dump=lambda exclude_none=True: d)
    c._c = NS(rulesets=NS(phases=NS(get=lambda ph, zone_id: NS(rules=[R(r) for r in rules]),
                                    update=lambda ph, zone_id, rules: calls.append((ph, rules)))))
    return c, calls

mine = [dict(ref='a', expression='true', action='set_cache_settings', action_parameters=dict(cache=True), enabled=True)]
theirs = dict(id='o1', ref='theirs', expression='true', action='block', enabled=True, version='3', last_updated='2026-10-19T00:00:00Z',
              logging=dict(enabled=False), ratelimit=dict(characteristics=['ip.src'], period=60, requests_per_period=10))
c, calls = fake_rules([theirs, dict(mine[0], id='v1', expression='false')])
test_eq(c.ruleset_upsert('z', mine), True)
(ph, sent), = calls
test_eq((ph, [r['ref'] for r in sent]), ('http_request_cache_settings', ['theirs', 'a']))
test_eq(sent[0], {k: v for k, v in theirs.items() if k not in ('version', 'last_updated')})   # a rule it does not own keeps its whole body
assert 'version' not in sent[0]
c, calls = fake_rules([theirs, dict(mine[0], id='v1')])
test_eq((c.ruleset_upsert('z', mine, phase='http_request_firewall_custom'), calls), (False, []))
logged = [dict(mine[0], logging=dict(enabled=False))]
c, calls = fake_rules([dict(mine[0], id='v1')])
test_eq(c.ruleset_upsert('z', logged), True)   # a change to a key of its own beyond the usual ones is a change
bare = [dict(ref='b', expression='true', action='set_cache_settings', action_parameters=dict(cache=True), description=None)]
stored = dict(bare[0], id='v2', version='1', last_updated='2026-10-19T00:00:00Z', enabled=True, description='')   # the API fills both in
c, calls = fake_rules([stored])
test_eq((c.ruleset_upsert('z', bare), calls), (False, []))
```

``` python
import httpx
from unittest import mock
from cloudflare import APIConnectionError, APITimeoutError, BadRequestError, InternalServerError, PermissionDeniedError, RateLimitError
_rq = httpx.Request('POST', 'https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/z/purge_cache')
def cf_err(cls, status, code, msg): return cls(msg, response=httpx.Response(status, request=_rq), body=dict(errors=[dict(code=code, message=msg)]))
refused = lambda: cf_err(PermissionDeniedError, 403, 10000, 'not on this plan')
def fake_purge(fails=None):
    'A client whose purge raises, for each kind of purge in `fails`, the errors listed there in turn, then succeeds; `calls` records each request.'
    c, calls, fails = CF('x'), [], {k: list(v) for k, v in (fails or {}).items()}
    def purge(zone_id, **kw):
        calls.append(kw)
        if (q := fails.get(first(kw))) and (e := q.pop(0)()): raise e
    c._c = NS(cache=NS(purge=purge))
    c._c.with_options = lambda **kw: c._c
    return c, calls

c, calls = fake_purge()
test_eq(c.purge('z', prefixes=['e.com/s/'], files=['https://e.com/']), [dict(files=['https://e.com/']), dict(prefixes=['e.com/s/'])])
test_eq(calls, [dict(files=['https://e.com/']), dict(prefixes=['e.com/s/'])])
c, calls = fake_purge(dict(prefixes=[refused]))
test_eq((c.purge('z', prefixes=['e.com/s/'], fallback_all=True), calls), ([dict(purge_everything=True)], [dict(prefixes=['e.com/s/']), dict(purge_everything=True)]))
c, calls = fake_purge(dict(prefixes=[refused]))
test_fail(lambda: c.purge('z', prefixes=['e.com/s/']), contains='not on this plan')
test_eq(calls, [dict(prefixes=['e.com/s/'])])   # the default sends no purge of everything
test_fail(lambda: fake_purge()[0].purge('z'), contains='purge needs')
test_eq(fake_purge()[0].purge('z', everything=True), [dict(purge_everything=True)])
```

``` python
# a refused prefixes purge after a files purge reports both; rate limits and timeouts retry after waits that double each time; any other error raises
c, calls = fake_purge(dict(prefixes=[refused]))
test_eq(c.purge('z', prefixes=['e.com/s/'], files=['https://e.com/'], fallback_all=True), [dict(files=['https://e.com/']), dict(purge_everything=True)])
waits, slow = [], lambda: cf_err(RateLimitError, 429, 1134, 'Unable to purge, rate limit reached')
with mock.patch('time.sleep', waits.append):
    c, calls = fake_purge(dict(prefixes=[slow, lambda: APITimeoutError(_rq)]))
    test_eq((c.purge('z', prefixes=['e.com/s/']), calls), ([dict(prefixes=['e.com/s/'])], [dict(prefixes=['e.com/s/'])] * 3))
    test_eq(waits, [1, 2])
    c, calls = fake_purge(dict(prefixes=[slow] * 4))
    test_fail(lambda: c.purge('z', prefixes=['e.com/s/'], tries=3), contains='rate limit')
    test_eq(len(calls), 3)   # no purge of everything after a rate limit
    c, calls = fake_purge(dict(prefixes=[lambda: cf_err(BadRequestError, 400, 1092, 'bad prefix'), lambda: 0]))
    test_fail(lambda: c.purge('z', prefixes=['https://e.com/s/']), contains='bad prefix')
    c, calls = fake_purge(dict(prefixes=[lambda: RuntimeError('socket closed'), lambda: 0]))
    test_fail(lambda: c.purge('z', prefixes=['e.com/s/']), contains='socket closed')
    test_eq(calls, [dict(prefixes=['e.com/s/'])])
```

The SDK client retries a connection error, a rate limit and an HTTP 5xx
response twice by default, and also HTTP 408 and 409. `purge` sends its
requests through a client with `max_retries=0`, so `tries` is the total
number of requests for one purge. `purge` retries all of these itself.
The cell below counts the requests that reach a stand-in HTTP transport.

``` python
sent = []
def too_many(request):
    sent.append(request.url.path)
    body = dict(success=False, errors=[dict(code=1134, message='Unable to purge, rate limit reached')], messages=[], result=None)
    return httpx.Response(429, json=body, headers={'retry-after-ms': '1'})
c = CF('x', http_client=httpx.Client(transport=httpx.MockTransport(too_many)))
test_fail(lambda: c.purge('z', files=['https://e.com/'], tries=3, wait=0), contains='rate limit')
test_eq(len(sent), 3)
sent
```

`purge` also retries a connection error, an HTTP 5xx response, HTTP 408
and HTTP 409, which the SDK client retried before `max_retries=0`, and
each retry counts against `tries`. The cell below sends a dropped
connection and a 502, 408 and 409 response through the stand-in
transport. Each purge makes `tries` requests and then raises.

``` python
def flaky(respond):
    sent = []
    def handler(request):
        sent.append(request.url.path)
        return respond(request)
    return sent, CF('x', http_client=httpx.Client(transport=httpx.MockTransport(handler)))
def drop(request): raise httpx.ConnectError('connection reset', request=request)
def status(code): return lambda request: httpx.Response(code, json=dict(success=False, errors=[], messages=[], result=None))
counts = {}
for name, respond, msg in [('connection error', drop, 'Connection error'), ('502', status(502), '502'), ('408', status(408), '408'), ('409', status(409), '409')]:
    sent, c = flaky(respond)
    test_fail(lambda: c.purge('z', files=['https://e.com/'], tries=3, wait=0), contains=msg)
    counts[name] = len(sent)
test_eq(counts, {'connection error': 3, '502': 3, '408': 3, '409': 3})
counts
```

An upsert touches only records of its own type. It keeps one record of
that type under the name: the first record with the requested `content`,
else the first record of that type. It updates the kept record in place
when its `content` or `proxied` setting differs. It deletes the other
records of that type under the name. It reads `api.internal` as a
subdomain of the zone. The lookup and the new record then share one full
name.

``` python
def rec(id, type, name, content, proxied=False): return NS(id=id, type=type, name=name, content=content, proxied=proxied, model_dump=lambda: dict(id=id, type=type, name=name, content=content, proxied=proxied))

c = fake_cf(); m = c._c
m.dns.records.list.side_effect = lambda zone_id, name: [rec('a', 'A', name, '1.1.1.1'), rec('t', 'TXT', name, 'v=spf1')]
m.dns.records.update.side_effect = lambda rid, **kw: rec(rid, kw['type'], kw['name'], kw['content'], kw['proxied'])
m.dns.records.create.side_effect = lambda **kw: rec('new', kw['type'], kw['name'], kw['content'], kw['proxied'])

c.upsert_record('example.com', 'www', '2.2.2.2')
test_eq(m.dns.records.delete.call_count, 0)
test_eq(m.dns.records.update.call_args.args, ('a',))

res = c.upsert_record('example.com', 'www', '1.1.1.1', proxied=True)
test_eq(res['proxied'], True)

c.upsert_record('example.com', 'api.internal', '3.3.3.3')
test_eq(m.dns.records.list.call_args.kwargs['name'], 'api.internal.example.com')
res
```

A CNAME cannot share a name with other address records, so
`tunnel_cname` first deletes the A and AAAA records at the name. It
leaves TXT, MX and every other type alone. An existing CNAME is updated
in place, or reduced to one, by `upsert_record`. The check below uses a
stand-in client that keeps its records in a list.

``` python
def fake_dns(*recs):
    c, store = fake_cf(), list(recs)
    def create(**kw): store.append(rec(f"n{len(store)}", kw['type'], kw['name'], kw['content'], kw['proxied'])); return store[-1]
    def delete(rid, zone_id): store[:] = [r for r in store if r.id != rid]
    c._c.dns.records.list.side_effect = lambda zone_id, name: [r for r in store if r.name == name]
    c._c.dns.records.create.side_effect = create
    c._c.dns.records.delete.side_effect = delete
    return c, store

c, store = fake_dns(rec('a', 'A', 'app.example.com', '1.1.1.1'), rec('aaaa', 'AAAA', 'app.example.com', '::1'), rec('t', 'TXT', 'app.example.com', 'v=spf1'), rec('o', 'A', 'other.example.com', '9.9.9.9'))
c.tunnel_cname('example.com', 'app', 'tid')
test_eq(sorted((r.type, r.name) for r in store), [('A', 'other.example.com'), ('CNAME', 'app.example.com'), ('TXT', 'app.example.com')])

c, store = fake_dns(rec('c1', 'CNAME', 'app.example.com', 'old.example.net'), rec('c2', 'CNAME', 'app.example.com', 'older.example.net'))
c.upsert_record('example.com', 'app', 'new.example.net', type='CNAME')
test_eq(len(store), 1)

c, store = fake_dns(rec('a1', 'A', 'example.com', '1.1.1.1'), rec('a2', 'A', 'example.com', '1.1.1.1'), rec('a3', 'A', 'example.com', '2.2.2.2'), rec('mx', 'MX', 'example.com', 'mail.example.com'))
c.upsert_record('example.com', 'example.com.', '1.1.1.1')
test_eq(sorted(r.id for r in store), ['a1', 'mx'])

c.upsert_record('example.com', '@', '3.3.3.3', type='TXT')
test_eq(sorted((r.type, r.name) for r in store), [('A', 'example.com'), ('MX', 'example.com'), ('TXT', 'example.com')])

c.tunnel_cname('example.com', 'example.com.', 'tid')
sorted((r.type, r.name) for r in store)
```

An error body whose `errors` is null still classifies, so the original
failure is what reaches the caller.

``` python
from cloudflare import APIStatusError
```

``` python
err = APIStatusError('bad', response=httpx.Response(400, request=httpx.Request('POST', 'https://x.test')), body={'errors': None})
test_eq(_purge_kind(err), None)
```

## Helpers

[`repo_root`](https://vedicreader.github.io/cfeasy/core.html#repo_root)
returns the top folder of the git repository you are working in, found
by walking up from the current directory until it finds a `.git` entry.
It returns None outside a repository.

cfeasy includes a `SKILL.md` file that tells coding agents such as
Claude Code how to use the library.
[`mv_skill_md`](https://vedicreader.github.io/cfeasy/core.html#mv_skill_md)
copies it into a project’s `.agents/skills/cfeasy/` and
`.claude/skills/cfeasy/` folders, where those agents look for skills. By
default it only prints where it would copy the file; pass
`dry_run=False` to copy it. The project root is `dir` if you give one,
otherwise the repository root, otherwise the current directory.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/cfeasy/blob/main/cfeasy/core.py#L192"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### mv_skill_md
